title: Attributing and Controlling Cost
description: Make each team see its own spend and stop runaway resources before the invoice arrives.

data.text: The subscription bill arrives and nobody can explain a $4,200 increase. It turns out a developer left a GPU virtual machine running over a holiday weekend and a test storage account accumulated three years of logs. Finance asks which team owns each resource; there is no answer in the portal.

Three layers: (1) enforce a **tagging policy** (`owner`, `environment`, `costCenter`, `project`) with Azure Policy so untagged resources cannot be created; (2) set **budgets with alert thresholds** per resource group and per team, so spend is visible during the month rather than after it; (3) add **automatic shutdown** for dev and test compute, plus a **lifecycle rule** on storage so logs expire instead of growing forever.

data.title: Budget with escalating alerts (Bicep)

data.text: Cost optimisation without attribution is guesswork: nobody has an incentive to turn off a resource they do not know they own. Tags turn the bill from one opaque number into a per-team scoreboard, and budgets turn months of silence into an alert while there is still time to act.
